references.text: Direct linguistic parallel: also uses the words 'rekev' (chariots) and 'parashim' (horsemen), here referring to Pharaoh's army that pursued Israel, similar to the great procession of chariots and horsemen in Genesis 50:9.
The immediate context describes who went up: Joseph's household, Pharaoh's servants, and the elders of Egypt, which explains why the camp was so large and heavy.
When Jacob went down to Egypt, Pharaoh sent chariots to carry him. Now at his burial, chariots and horsemen accompany again, forming a frame around Jacob's stay in Egypt.
Theological contrast: Genuine Egyptian military forces honoring God's man (Joseph) versus those same forces punishing God's people.
